guard: membership reads and caller-owned watches recover across manual and terminal reconnects, with one broker consumer per live watch and no predecessor leak
why: The live pre-fix reproduction proves the stale membership-feed cache fails after reconnect; the pinned client aborts that path after the named read failure, so it is not misreported as a mutation kill.

The three completing mutations isolate watch rearm, caller-stop broker deletion, and fresh-connection cleanup after terminal close. The rejected-chain recovery cell remains as a direct regression: clearConnectionScoped is the single reset point, so a second mutation on the downstream append would grade redundant code rather than another property.

mutations.name: reconnect drops the membership watch rearm call
mutations.expectRed: the membership feed watch stays live across reconnect
mutations.cell: the membership feed watch stays live across reconnect
mutations.note: The old iterator is retired and the intent never gets a successor, so the post-reconnect membership-rw write produces no callback.

mutations.name: stopping a membership watch leaves its ordered broker consumer
mutations.expectRed: stopping the membership watch deletes its broker consumer
mutations.cell: stopping the membership watch deletes its broker consumer
mutations.note: The caller stop has no later rearm, so local iterator stop alone leaves the ordered consumer until its inactivity threshold.

mutations.name: terminal self-heal forgets the closed-epoch consumer identity before fresh cleanup
mutations.expectRed: terminal self-heal creates one successor and deletes the closed-epoch predecessor
mutations.cell: terminal self-heal creates one successor and deletes the closed-epoch predecessor
mutations.note: Old-connection deletion cannot run after nc.closed. The fresh connection must delete the recorded stream/name before creating the successor.
